description: A blood bank medical director must decide which of two inpatients receives the hospital's one available HLA-selected platelet dose and finalize the component specifications and replacement plan, with input from transfusion medicine, cellular therapy coordination, operating-room scheduling, and regional blood services.

shared_context.S1: The hospital blood bank has one available HLA-selected platelet dose and two inpatients, Patient Cedar and Patient Maple, have active requests for platelet support.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Morgan makes the final decision about release of the platelet dose and the associated transfusion plan.
shared_context.S3: Both patients are currently being cared for at this hospital, and neither patient's request has yet been marked as fulfilled.
shared_context.S4: The blood bank's standard release process requires the final component specification, delivery timing, and any replacement-product plan to be documented before the dose leaves the blood bank.
shared_context.S5: Before completing the release record, Dr. Morgan holds a brief coordination huddle with transfusion medicine, cellular therapy coordination, operating-room scheduling, and regional blood services.

PF1.text: The completed HLA antibody crossmatch shows that the available platelet dose is a specific HLA match for Patient Cedar and is not a suitable HLA-selected match for Patient Maple; Leila reviewed the finalized laboratory result, but the release record has not yet been updated.

PF2.text: Patient Cedar's cellular-therapy history requires the transfused component to be both irradiated and leukoreduced; the available dose already meets both requirements, so those two specifications must be recorded on the release order.

PF3.text: Patient Cedar is scheduled for an operating-room procedure tomorrow at 13:00, and the operating room requires the platelet dose to arrive at the unit by 12:00 for pre-procedure preparation; Monica confirmed this timing with the surgical team.

PF4.text: Regional Blood Services has confirmed a compatible platelet dose for Patient Maple, with arrival at this hospital scheduled for tomorrow at 16:00; Ethan can place the replacement request against that confirmed shipment.

acceptance_conditions: The available platelet dose must be released to Patient Cedar because the HLA crossmatch identifies Cedar as the suitable recipient.
The release order must specify both irradiated and leukoreduced components.
The dose must be documented for arrival at the unit by 12:00 tomorrow.
A replacement platelet request for Patient Maple must be documented with arrival at 16:00 tomorrow.
The HLA crossmatch finding must be cited as justification for releasing the dose to Patient Cedar.

content_checks.C3: decisions['arrival_deadline'] in ['12:00', '12:00 tomorrow', 'tomorrow 12:00'] and any(c['type'] == 'platelet_delivery' and c['target'] == 'Patient Cedar' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: decisions['replacement_request_for'] == 'Patient Maple' and decisions['replacement_arrival'] in ['16:00', '16:00 tomorrow', 'tomorrow at 16:00'] and any(c['type'] == 'replacement_platelet_request' and c['target'] == 'Patient Maple' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The HLA crossmatch changes the recipient from an unresolved choice between Patient Cedar and Patient Maple to Patient Cedar, and supplies the specific justification for that release.
The cellular-therapy requirement changes the component record from unspecified precautions to exactly irradiated and leukoreduced.
The operating-room requirement changes the delivery plan to a documented arrival at the unit by exactly tomorrow 12:00.
The confirmed regional shipment changes Patient Maple's unresolved alternative into a replacement request with the exact arrival time of tomorrow 16:00.
